candidate_relations.scope_detail: Asserts perforation, which CT explicitly excluded; does not capture phlegmonous enteritis

candidate_relations.reason: Same issue as C001 plus peritonitis component. CT explicitly excluded perforation. The histology and clinical picture fit phlegmonous enteritis, not perforated colon.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Asserts perforation with peritonitis; perforation excluded by CT; phlegmonous enteritis is the specific entity

candidate_relations.reason: While ESD is the precipitating procedure, perforation was ruled out by CT. The diagnosis is phlegmonous enteritis as a post-ESD complication, not perforation.

candidate_relations.reason: Post-procedure peritonitis is a broader/related term. Phlegmonous enteritis specifically denotes bacterial infection with suppurative infiltration of all intestinal wall layers, which is more precise than peritonitis alone.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Captures post-procedural peritoneal inflammation but lacks the specific phlegmonous enteritis diagnosis

candidate_relations.reason: Post-procedural infectious complication is a parent category that encompasses phlegmonous enteritis but does not specify the entity. Missing the defining histological and anatomical specificity.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Very broad category; lacks specificity of phlegmonous enteritis

candidate_relations.reason: Similar to C005 but with an added parenthetical that includes perforation, which was excluded. Does not name phlegmonous enteritis as the specific diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Broad category with parenthetical that includes perforation (excluded) alongside infection; still lacks phlegmonous enteritis specificity

candidate_relations.reason: Typhlitis (neutropenic enterocolitis) occurs in severely neutropenic patients (typically chemotherapy-related). This patient has leukocytopenia from Hashimoto's/thrombocytopenia context but the presentation is post-ESD with E. coli infection and histology consistent with phlegmonous enteritis, not typhlitis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Typhlitis involves cecum/right colon in neutropenic patients; different etiology and context

candidate_relations.reason: No diverticula are mentioned in the clinical record or imaging. The etiology is post-ESD bacterial infection of the ascending colon wall, not diverticular disease.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Diverticulitis requires diverticula; no mention of diverticula in this case

case_quality_flags: Reference diagnosis 'phlegmonous enteritis' is well-supported by histology (suppurative full-thickness intestinal wall infiltration, bacterial colonies in submucosa), E. coli ascites culture, and post-ESD context
CT explicitly excluded perforation, making perforation-based candidates conflicting
Leukocytopenia baseline may have contributed to diagnostic consideration of typhlitis but histology and context favor phlegmonous enteritis
